title: Creative portfolio for visual work
when: The user wants a portfolio for visual work: design, illustration, art, architecture or photography.
inputs: projects with images and short descriptions
prompt:
Goal: Let the work speak: a fast grid of projects, a short intro and an easy way to get in touch.
Steps:
1. Intro in two lines: name, discipline and the kind of clients or projects wanted.
2. Project grid with consistent aspect ratios; each card has an image, title, year and a one line role.
3. A detail section per highlighted project: problem, approach, result, and two or three images.
4. About block with a short bio and the services offered.
5. Contact with email link and availability; no forms unless asked.
Quality bar:
- Images have width, height and descriptive alt text.
- Grid stays readable at 375 px (one column) and fills wide screens.
- Typography is restrained so the images lead.
Pitfalls:
- Autoplay sliders that hide most of the work.
- Enormous uncompressed images.
- Clever navigation labels nobody understands.
Verify:
- [ ] Every img has alt, width and height.
- [ ] Images after the first load lazily.
- [ ] Keyboard focus is visible on every card link.
- [ ] One h1.
Output: index.html with intro, grid, project details and contact; style.css with a responsive grid.

examples.input: portfolio for an illustrator named Bia
examples.output: grid of 6 projects with year and role, a case study for a book cover, email link
